overall: Tomorrow (Monday, June 23) in Atlanta brings partly sunny skies with a 30% chance of showers and thunderstorms developing after 11am, driven by a southwest flow with gusts to 25 mph. The NWS text forecast calls for a high near 89°F, though ensemble model probabilities cluster considerably lower in the lower-to-mid 80s, likely reflecting the anchoring effect of the cool prior-day observed max of 77°F. A flood warning is active in southeast Georgia (Satilla River, Brantley County) — this is remote from Atlanta and carries no direct bearing on tomorrow's Atlanta temperature outlook.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is notably wide: NBM leads at 86.4°F and GFS is the outlier low at 80.7°F, while ECMWF (84.3°F), HRRR (82.9°F), and WEATHER_COM (82.1°F) cluster in the mid-range. max_temp_prediction: The full ensemble expected TMAX is 80.6°F, with the two highest-probability buckets tied at 80-81°F and 82-83°F (20.4% each), placing the most likely high in the 80-83°F range. The NWS narrative at 89°F and NBM at 86.4°F represent the warmer tail, but those are less supported by the ensemble bucket distribution. Confidence is low — both bucket sets are rated Tier 4 (Poor signals, AVOID) with expected accuracy of only ~32%, and inter-model spread exceeds 5°F, so this forecast carries significant uncertainty.
